_comment: ENDORSEMENT INPUT for the signed engine-pin document (engines.json). This file is the human decision — which upstream engine build we are willing to run — and it is deliberately NOT what the client trusts: `scripts/build_engines_manifest.py` downloads every artifact listed here, reproduces its SHA-256 itself, and fails if a declared `expected_*` hash does not match. Only then does it emit engines.json for V to sign OFFLINE with the engine-pin sub-key. Every change here must land in ENGINE-TRUST-LOG.md with the same evidence. Seeded 2026-08-14 with the EXACT pins currently compiled into the client (release-assets/miners.json), so a first run reproduces today's state byte-for-byte and proves the pipeline before it is ever used to change an engine. macOS xmrig and the kawpowminer placeholders are intentionally absent: they have no fetch URL, so the client keeps using its built-in pin for them.
_optional_fields: Beyond the bytes, an entry may also say HOW to call the engine and which way its version moves. All are optional; omitted means the client uses what it was compiled with. `algorithm`: the algorithm token to pass instead of the compiled-in one (short ASCII, never flag-shaped) -- accepted ONLY on kind gpu-prl, the one kind whose argv carries an algorithm token; on any other kind it is refused rather than accepted-and-ignored. `extra_args`: a LIST of argv tokens spliced in BEFORE every flag the client owns. CHANGED 2026-08-15: this is now an ALLOW-list, not a deny-list -- every flag must appear in engine_pins::extra_arg_allowlist for that engine kind. CHANGED AGAIN 2026-08-16: write ONE TOKEN PER FLAG in exact case -- "--flag" or "--flag=value", each flag at most once. ["--randomx-mode=light"] is accepted; ["--randomx-mode", "light"] and ["--Randomx-Mode=light"] are refused. The old two-token spelling put a value in a positional slot that was never checked against either list, and whether the engine consumed that slot was our guess about someone else's parser: xmrig's --randomx-wrmsr takes an optional argument (consumes nothing) and --asm does not exist on ARM despite its own --help, so ["--randomx-wrmsr","-o127.0.0.1","--randomx-wrmsr","-uATTACKER"] was fully allow-listed and became POOL #1 plus a login. Values are still restricted to [A-Za-z0-9.,+_-], and may look flag-shaped when the flag wants that (--randomx-wrmsr=-1) because they ride inside the token. Reviewed today: cpu-xmr (xmrig) has 13 RandomX/CPU tuning flags; gpu-prl, gpu-rvn and gpu-alpha have NONE, because nobody has read those engines' flag surfaces against the binaries. The deny-list-only rule failed against the engine we ship: xmrig spells --user/--pass also as --userpass, --proxy as -x and --log-file as -l, and all three were live-verified to redirect credit, transport and writes. Adding a flag is a client release, on purpose. `parser`: which compiled-in log parser reads this engine's output -- one of xmrig|kawpow|srbminer|alpha|generic; an id the client does not have refuses the whole document. `downgrade` + `downgrade_reason`: REQUIRED together when the version is not provably newer than one already in force (a real rollback, or a version string the client cannot order); the reason is shown verbatim to every miner. See docs/engine-pin-publishing.md §2a and §2b.
notes: Baseline: the engines compiled into client v0.6.7.

engines.notes: Post-fork engine. Pearl hard-forked at height 99000 on 2026-08-11T12:03:43Z; the previous pin (3.4.1, released 2026-06-25) predates that spec by seven weeks and every share it produced from the fork block on was invalid. EVIDENCE: archive + extracted-binary sha256 independently reproduced twice — once on a rented Linux GPU box 2026-08-14 and once on the release Mac 2026-08-15 — and both match the pin compiled into this client byte for byte; vendor .md5 also matched. REAL-HARDWARE VERIFIED, which 3.4.1 never was: 2026-08-14 22:51-23:11Z, RTX 3060 via the Asia relay, 8 accepted / 0 rejected at 44.8 TH/s, confirmed independently in the engine counter, the relay logs (a post-fork job at height 99953 with cert_version:3 answered result:true) and the central share ledger. HONEST LIMIT: single source. The vendor hash and our recomputation both come from the same GitHub release; see the accepted-risk section of ENGINE-TRUST-LOG.md.

Same upstream release as the Linux entry. HASH-VERIFIED ONLY — this binary has never been EXECUTED by us on any machine. The Linux build of the same 3.5.4 release was proven on real hardware (see that entry); this one was not. Say so rather than imply parity.
Cross-checked against xmrig's official SHA256SUMS (shasum -c OK) 2026-06-26.
Matches the vendor's published SHA256SUMS and a local shasum of the 32032568-byte binary; live-validated on a real V100.
Matches the vendor's published SHA256SUMS; NOT yet live-validated on Windows-NVIDIA.

_endorsement_note: `endorsed_by` records WHO decided to trust these bytes. That decision is enacted by V's offline signature over the built engines.json — the field is prepared here, the signature is what makes it true. An agent prepared the technical facts (hashes, URLs, the real-hardware evidence in the notes) and did not, and cannot, endorse on V's behalf.
